problems.title: Proposition 6.3 classifies a broader set than its eight representatives cover
problems.source_claim: All merotropic subspaces of E3, up to S8 and orthogonal complement, belong to eight listed types.
assumptions: E3 even subsets of eight letters modulo complement, pairing intersection parity
problems.complete_check: X radical=Y and restricted rank=2, so X is non-isotropic and merotropic. Its orthogonal-pair dimension/rank signature {(2,0),(4,2)} differs from every listed pair; listed 2D representatives are nondegenerate with signatures {(2,2),(4,4)}. S8 preserves these invariants.
problems.counterevidence: Definition 6.4 explicitly uses the smaller-dimensional merotropic member. Our pair is excluded there since its smaller member Y is isotropic dimension2. No failure of that actual downstream domain follows.
problems.impact: Local classification scope defect; no demonstrated failure of compatible-subspace machinery or geometric conjecture.

correction.statement: Restrict classification to orthogonal pairs whose smaller-dimensional member is merotropic, with complementation identification for dim3.
correction.result: Independent enumeration gives 8 S8 orbits: sizes 1; 28,35; 56,280; 35,280,315 for dimensions0,1,2,3. All Table8 complements and radicals independently checked.
